turn off verb

a tap

classical

1Not Traupman’s versāre / reversāre (Traupman 123); reversāre is Late Latin. A house ruling. Ruling: Turning a tap on and off.

epitonium claudere1

turn the tap off

Other words

  • aquam sistere — turn the water off

    also used · classical

Examples

  • «Satis est,» inquit. «Siste aquam.» Puer epitonium ipse clausit.

    “That’s enough,” he said. “Turn the water off.” The boy turned the tap off himself.composed

See also turn on, tap.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 123.
